title: Give the lights instructions
problem: Make the first light orange and the last light blue.
idea: Instructions run in order. Pixel numbers begin at 0.
predict: If you paint the same light twice, which colour will you see?
task: Keep the orange light and add a blue light at count minus 1.
extension: Add a white light halfway along the strip. Try 25 and 100 lights.
bug: The broken version uses count as a position. The last valid position is count minus 1.
check: At 1 pixel, blue wins because it is drawn last. At 25 pixels, positions 0 and 24 are lit.
explain: Point to the instruction that draws first, and explain why the last position needs minus 1.

title: Name what changes
problem: Change several lights together without hunting for repeated colour numbers.
idea: A variable is a name for a value. Set a name before reading it.
predict: Does changing colour after drawing the first light repaint that light?
task: Give the colour a name, then use that name at both ends.
extension: Give the middle light a second colour. Change only one name to try a new theme.
bug: The broken version changes a colour into a number. Keep a name the same kind of value.
check: Both ends use the same colour. On a one-pixel strip the last instruction wins.
explain: Say what colour holds immediately before each drawing instruction.

title: Repeat a useful action
problem: Paint a changing band of colour on any strip length without copying instructions.
idea: A loop repeats its body once for each position. All those writes make one frame.
predict: List the position values for a strip with five lights.
task: Make the red amount grow with position: 60 times position divided by count.
extension: Paint every other light blue. Keep the growing red colour on the others.
bug: The broken loop takes one step too many and tries to draw outside the strip.
check: Try 25, 31, 32, 33 and 100 lights. The end stays below red 60.
explain: Explain why a loop through the lights is not an animation by itself.

title: Make a choice
problem: Split the strip into coloured sections, with a warning colour near the end.
idea: A condition chooses which instructions to run. Only one side of if/else runs.
predict: Which colour appears exactly at the halfway point?
task: Add a red section from three quarters of the strip to the end.
extension: Add a small white marker at the halfway point.
bug: The broken version reverses the comparison. It runs, but paints the sections the wrong way round.
check: Use an odd count such as 25. Explain which side gets the extra light.
explain: Describe each condition in words before reading the code.

title: Make time visible
problem: Make a light blink once per second while the controls stay usable.
idea: The frame function is called again and again. Elapsed time tells us which picture to draw now.
predict: What should be visible at 0, 0.999, 1 and 2 seconds?
task: Use elapsed whole seconds to choose between orange and dark.
extension: Replace the sudden change with a slow rise and fall in brightness.
bug: The broken version repeats forever inside one frame. No complete frame reaches the lights.
check: Try time steps of 0, 0.033, 0.25 and 1 second. A time step of 0 should not change the picture.
explain: Explain why you do not need a forever loop or a sleep instruction here.

title: Remember movement
problem: Move a dot at the same speed even when some frames arrive late.
idea: Remembered values survive the next frame. Seconds since the last frame tells us how far to move.
predict: At 8 pixels per second, how far does the dot move in a quarter of a second?
task: Add elapsed seconds times speed to the remembered position, then wrap at the end.
extension: Use a speed of minus 8 to travel backwards around the ring.
bug: The broken version moves one pixel per frame. It changes speed when the frame time changes.
check: Run at 0.016 and 0.25 seconds per frame. Compare distance after the same total time.
explain: Explain the difference between a local position and state.position.

title: Give an idea a name
problem: Use one colour rule in several places without copying it.
idea: A function receives values through its input names. A calculation gives back a value; a drawing function carries out instructions.
predict: What changes if you change the colour rule in just one place?
task: Make a calculation that chooses orange or blue, and a drawing function that paints a marker.
extension: Add a second marker using the same drawing function.
bug: The broken calculation forgets its else choice. Give colour a value whichever choice runs.
check: Change the split from one half to one quarter. Every use of the rule should change together.
explain: Point out the supplied values, the function’s input names, and the returned colour.

title: Make it adjustable
problem: Move a progress bar without editing and restarting the program.
idea: A live input can change between frames. A starting setting is read when the program starts.
predict: How many lights should be orange at progress 0, 0.5 and 1?
task: Replace the fixed halfway value with the progress input.
extension: Add a warning colour when progress is at least 0.8. Try a starting setting for the warning point.
bug: The broken version uses progress plus 1 as an array position. A progress value is not a pixel position.
check: Use the progress control after a frame finishes. Test exactly 0 and 1. A saved value is used again after restart; choose the default in Preview settings & inputs to restore it.
explain: Explain why an input changes during playback while a setting needs restart.

title: Remember several values
problem: Give each light its own brightness and change one without changing the rest.
idea: An array holds several values. Its position and the value stored there are different things.
predict: If the value at position 0 is 0.2, which number says where to draw and which says how bright?
task: Create the brightness array once, change its first value, and read it while drawing.
extension: Fade every stored brightness value using the time since the last frame.
bug: The broken version forgot to create the array. Create it once in the starting section.
check: Change one entry and then the last entry. Run at 25 and 100 pixels without changing the array length by hand.
explain: Explain why changing one array entry survives until the next frame.

title: Stop when done
problem: Find a free light, including when no lights are free.
idea: A while loop repeats until its condition becomes false. Check the array length before reading an entry.
predict: Where should the search stop when every entry is already used?
task: Walk forward while the slot is used, then paint it only if it is inside the array.
extension: Start with every slot filled. Show a white strip when the search finds no free slot.
bug: The broken search never advances its slot. The first frame works; the next frame gets stuck.
check: Run enough frames to fill the strip. The search must finish both before and after the final slot is filled.
explain: Explain why checking slot < count comes before reading used[slot].

title: Give lights a life
problem: Make small lights appear, fade and leave room for the next ones.
idea: Choose a random place once per new light. A seed lets you replay those choices. A saved image remembers the trail.
predict: Will asking for a random place inside every pixel loop make one firefly or many unrelated choices?
task: Choose a new place every 0.2 seconds and fade the old lights by elapsed time.
extension: Replace the random place with a moving place that wraps around the ring.
bug: The broken version uses a negative fade rate. The trail stays bright instead of fading.
check: Restart twice: the first random choices should match. Try a delayed frame. A long delay creates at most one new light.
explain: Explain the difference between one random choice per new light and one per drawn pixel. Stored colour steps round, and fast movement can skip pixels.

title: Make a small installation
problem: Build a lighthouse beam that crosses the ring seam, then explain how it works.
idea: Combine movement, loops, conditions and a named drawing function. Test a change before adding another.
predict: When the beam reaches position 0, where do its trailing lights go?
task: Move a three-light beam around the ring. Keep its speed in pixels per second.
extension: Add a second beam halfway around the ring, using the same drawing function.
bug: The broken version forgets to wrap the trailing lights. It fails when the beam crosses the first pixel.
check: Try 1, 12, 25 and 100 pixels; reverse speed; use a one-second frame delay. Explain overlapping writes on a very short ring.
explain: Find one loop, one condition, one changing value and one function. Describe an improvement and how you would test it.
